title: Philippine Energy Security Could Determine the Outcome of a Taiwan Contingency
gist: Steven Bancroft argues Philippine fuel insecurity is a decades-old weakness in US strategy: a Taiwan conflict would likely disrupt the oil imports sustaining US operations from the Philippines (truncated excerpt).

insights.claim: In March the Philippines declared a 'state of energy emergency' after crude delivery disruptions, and Petron, its only refinery, bought Russian oil after a US waiver.
insights.speaker: Steven Bancroft
insights.so_what: Even a US ally needed sanctions waivers to secure crude, exposing supply fragility.

insights.claim: Philippine fuel insecurity is a decades-old vulnerability in US strategy.
insights.speaker: Steven Bancroft
insights.so_what: Energy logistics in the Philippines is a hidden constraint on US Indo-Pacific posture.

insights.claim: To deter China from a Taiwan annexation attempt, the US needs access to the Philippines and its oil, but a conflict drawing in the US would likely disrupt the Philippine oil imports that sustain American operations.
insights.speaker: Steven Bancroft
insights.so_what: Fuel supply security in the Philippines could determine wartime outcomes; relevant to regional refining, shipping and fuel storage investment.
